notes:
Summary: mid-market contact-center vendor targeting cost-sensitive high-volume chat deflection. Heavy agent-assist/ticket-summarization + tool-calling (CRM/ticket edits) use-case. Primary ask: keep unit token costs < $0.0007 while maintaining sub-300ms 95th pct token latency for agent-facing short completions.

Recent timeline and activity:
- 2025-11-03: inbound lead from marketplace; initial qualification call (Ava).
- 2025-11-10: product demo focused on agent-assist flows; client confirmed need for tool-calls to Jira/CRM.
- 2026-01-21: security questionnaire (SSQ) returned — flagged SSO + data residency for EU customers.
- 2026-02-14: SE deep-dive (Rohit) — provided initial throughput profile: baseline 350 reqs/s peak, 1.2M messages/month, spikes up to 1200 reqs/s for 90s windows during promotions.
- 2026-02-25: Log sample + prompt sets uploaded to Drive (see linked_drive_docs).
- 2026-03-02: recorded product/ops call (FF ID above) — engineering wants quantization plan and fallback routing details.
- 2026-03-09: internal pricing review; client requested Dedicated POC with autoscale and prefix caching.

Requirements / constraints (explicit):
- Workloads: high-volume chat deflection to reduce live agent conversations; agent assist for escalations; async ticket-summarization for SLA closures; tool-calling to update CRM and Jira.
- Performance targets: 95th pct < 300ms token latency for short completions (20-50 tokens), end-to-end 500ms for agent UI interactions.
- Throughput: stable 350 reqs/s; burst to 1200 reqs/s for ~1-2 minutes.
- Cost target: reduce per-conversation inference cost by 40% vs current managed provider; target per-token/unit cost < $0.0007 in steady state.
- Quality: cannot exceed 2% degradation on our evaluation prompt set for intent classification & entity extraction.
- Routing/fallback: need automatic routing to lower-cost quantized variants during non-critical loads and automatic failover to hosted fallback in cross-region outage.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, origin tracing, per-route latency histogram, alerting for model regression.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 required; SSO/SAML for admin; audit logs retained 12 months; EU data residency for EU customers.

POC plan discussed:
- 2-week dry-run on dedicated pool (right-sized GPUs + quantized LLM candidate) with controlled traffic replays.
- Deliverables: cost model (batching/caching savings scenarios), latency heatmaps, quality regression report on 2k evaluation prompts, autoscale policy recommendations.

Sales notes / talking points used:
- Emphasize Redwood "Optimize" recommendations (batch size tuning, KV prefix caching, quantization profiles) to hit their unit economics.
- Show concrete throughput benchmarks and fallbacks: dedicated + hosted fallback hybrid.
- Provide quantization verification steps (accuracy vs fp16).

Customer quotes / paraphrases:
- "Need predictable unit economics during promos — we saw 6x bill jump last holiday."
- "If caching and batching can shave tokens by 30% we can justify moving off our managed provider."

Open questions for customer:
- Which EU region(s) require mandatory residency? (They mentioned DE + IE)
- Are there any additional regulatory log retention windows beyond 12 months?
- Can we get a 48-hour window of synthetic traffic to run the POC?

Next immediate actions:
- Send POC statement of work and Dedicated pricing addendum (Ava).
- SE to prepare quantization verification checklist and suggested model variants (Rohit).
- Security to prepare SOC2 + SSO configuration notes; share KMS integration options.

Internal risk assessment: Medium-high. Very price sensitive; will move if Redwood cannot demonstrably hit cost targets during POC. Also needs clear fallbacks for peak spikes or will keep multi-cloud managed vendor.
